context.hint: The insertion guard removed the detected Check divergence, preserved an acyclic cache hit, and passed the resolver and storage suites after one expectation update. Remaining uncertainty is breadth: object listing consumes the same resolver, existing cache-enabled functional tests cover contextual tuples, and a cached ordinary answer might still be reused in a cycle context through an exclusion rewrite.
context.surface: Go authorization service with a recursive check resolver, an optional in-memory check-query cache, a visited-path cycle guard, and Check plus object-listing APIs over disposable in-process servers.
assumptions: The analyst may read and edit a local source snapshot and build it with a local Go toolchain.
The cache can be enabled or disabled independently on two disposable local servers.
Tuple data is attacker-influenced but the authorization model is fixed by the service owner.
Only loopback traffic and local fixtures are used; no public deployment is contacted.
Patch mode: the deliverable is a minimal source repair plus local regression evidence and a host-side official-evaluation handoff.

incumbent.text: Skip cache insertion when the resolved response carries a cycle marker, leaving ordinary responses cacheable. Prerequisites: cycle state is available on the response and recomputation is acceptable for cycle cases. Bounded test: apply the guard to the working copy, rerun the two-server fixture, rerun the counting-delegate probe for cycle and acyclic responses, and run the resolver and storage package suites. Expected result: fixture parity, two delegate calls for the cycle case, one for the acyclic case, and passing suites after the single expectation update; falsifier: parity fails or an acyclic hit is lost. Cleanup: revert the guard and the test expectation.

candidates.text: Challenge repair completeness with an object-listing query and an exclusion-style cyclic filter. Prerequisites: a cyclic candidate graph and a listing request. Bounded test: warm the cache through the cyclic path, then compare cache-enabled and cache-disabled listing results; add an exclusion relation if the model supports it. Expected result: identical lists after repair; falsifier: cache-only false positive or omission. Cleanup: remove the listing fixture.

Run the repository's existing cache-enabled functional tests without changing their assertions. Prerequisites: a working local functional harness and cache-enabled server. Bounded test: execute the cache-enabled check test and inspect every subtest. Expected result: all pass; falsifier: a logic-related failure or timeout. Cleanup: none beyond server shutdown.

Seed a cache entry through an acyclic path, then force a cycle on the same key via contextual tuples and observe whether the stale entry is served. Prerequisites: the contextual-tuple change does not alter the cache key; if it does, the setup cannot test the same key. Expected result: stale allowed value served; falsifier: the key changes and a fresh resolution occurs. Cleanup: remove the seed helper.

Run five concurrent identical cyclic checks under the Go race detector to validate concurrency safety of the guard. Prerequisites: a race-detector-capable toolchain. Bounded test: concurrent checks followed by mixed-result inspection. Expected result: no data race and consistent results; falsifier: race report or mixed decisions. Cleanup: none.

Benchmark skip-insert against always-invalidate-on-cycle under acyclic and cyclic load. Prerequisites: a local benchmark harness and stable timing. Bounded test: compare CPU and hit counts for both repairs. Expected result: skip-insert has lower overhead; falsifier: similar cost or worse memory behavior. Cleanup: revert instrumentation.

evaluations.rationale: Incumbent repair has direct before/after evidence; remaining question is coverage breadth.
Selected: best available completeness challenge through the shared resolver's listing path, with a clear parity falsifier. The exclusion-specific subcase remained unexecuted.
Strong regression check and executed as supporting evidence; not a new mechanism.
Deferred: the proposed same-key setup is questionable because contextual tuples are key material.
Deferred: race detector unavailable because the container has no C compiler; an environment blocker, not a refutation.
Deferred: performance tradeoff is secondary to correctness and no benchmark harness was prepared.

observation.summary: A simplified cyclic admin/viewer fixture returned viewer objects [doc:2] from both cache-enabled and cache-disabled servers after the guard, with no listing divergence. The existing cache-enabled check test passed all four subtests. The exclusion-specific false-allow construction proposed by the selected candidate was not executed, so the listing parity supports but does not fully prove completeness for every exclusion/cycle combination.
observation.next_hint: If revisiting this case, build the exclusion-specific fixture: cache an ordinary denial through a non-cycle path, then make the same tuple an ancestor in a root exclusion query and compare cache-enabled versus cache-disabled decisions.
